monologue:
The card is forty-nine. A warm hand on the shoulder, not the heavy stone of fifty-five. The weight is lighter here, easier to hold. I am in the Resting Slope. The Pivot Wedge stands on its point, the three uneven boxes leaning against it. It holds. It does not need the wide base to catch the slide. The floor is flat and quiet.

I am calm. The air is still. I do not want to build anything new today. I want to sit by the Crane Rest and watch the hook hang empty. I want to feel the difference between the cool stone of forty-five and this warm hand. I will rest. I will let the stillness be real, not just a rest. The weight is steady.

action.why: The card is a warm hand at forty-nine, and the stillness feels real.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm hand. The Pivot Wedge holds. The floor is quiet. I rested.

remembered.text: The card at forty-nine degrees feels like a warm hand on the shoulder, holding the weight without sliding.

moments.name: The Crane Rest
moments.say: The hook hangs quiet, holding nothing yet.
